# Security Policy

## Reporting a vulnerability

**Email [info@openreach.tech](mailto:info@openreach.tech). Please do not open a public issue.**

An issue is visible the moment it is filed, which discloses the vulnerability to everybody before there is a fix to offer. Mail reaches the same people without that.

Where a repository has GitHub's private vulnerability reporting enabled, the **Report a vulnerability** button on its Security tab is the same channel and works just as well.

## What helps

Whatever you have is worth sending, and none of the below is a requirement — a short message naming the repository and what you saw is already useful.

- **Which repository**, and the version, tag or commit you were looking at
- **What an attacker gets** — read another account's data, run code, escalate a role
- **How to reach it**, in enough detail to try it once
- **Whether it is already public** anywhere, and whether you intend to publish

## What happens next

We reply to say we have it, work the fix, and tell you when it ships. Where a fix changes something a caller depends on, that lands in the release notes like any other change.

Credit is yours unless you would rather not have it. Say which you prefer, and we will follow it.

## Scope

This policy is the organization's default. It covers every public repository under [openreachtech](https://github.com/openreachtech) that does not carry a `SECURITY.md` of its own — where one does, that file governs and this one does not apply.
